column2: a decorative frame or outline drawn around a page, a box or a sidebar. NOT a margin, a limit or a country boundary.
an index tab printed on the outer edge of the page showing a book's name, so readers can find that book quickly (like the thumb index of a dictionary). NOT a thumbnail picture and NOT a thumb.
the Scripture book currently selected/displayed in the Paratext editor (or viewer). "Book" here is a Bible book, e.g. Mark.
one of the ruled horizontal lines in a wide outer margin that give readers room to write personal notes (as in a "journaling Bible"). NOT a line of footnotes.
how far (in %) a text colour may differ from the chosen spot colour and still be treated as that colour.
the bound edge of a book where the pages are joined, shown on the cover. NOT a backbone.
the vertical space left after a paragraph (paragraph spacing). NOT a space character.
the vertical space left before a paragraph (paragraph spacing). NOT a space character.
text formatting: a line drawn under the text.
the inner space between a box's contents and its border.
the extra inner margin next to the binding, where the pages are bound together.
extra printed area beyond the trim edge of the page so that colour reaches the cut edge.
the empty rectangle (a missing-character box) shown when a font lacks a character.
a chosen part of a book (a range of chapters or verses) that is typeset.
the small symbol or letter in the text (such as a, b, † or *) that points to a footnote or cross-reference.
a list of paragraph adjustments (expand or shrink a paragraph by one line at a given verse) used to balance columns and fix page endings.
the front matter and back matter of a publication: title page, copyright page, table of contents, maps, etc.
a straight horizontal line used as a separator or decoration (footnote rule, header rule). NOT a regulation.
a USFM code that starts with a backslash (such as \toc3 or \m) and tags the kind of text. Keep the code itself unchanged.
two translations printed side by side on the same page.
three or more translations printed side by side.
decorative graphics (flourishes, patterned borders).
a boxed panel of text or graphics placed beside or inside the text columns (for example a study-note panel).
the system of numbering chapters and verses, which differs between Bible versions.
breaking a word with a hyphen at the end of a line.
align text flush with both the left and the right margin.
a named, saved set of PTXprint settings for a project.
a layout where facing pages are mirror images, using inner and outer margins instead of left and right.
the pages before the Scripture text (title, copyright, contents).
the pages after the Scripture text (glossary, maps, indexes).
a second font used for characters that the main font does not contain.
a pointer in the text to a related Bible passage elsewhere.
